title: Coupang vs. e.l.f. Beauty: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares two consumer growth stocks: Coupang, a South Korean e-commerce and logistics giant with 25 million users, and e.l.f. Beauty, a viral cosmetics brand. While Coupang trades at a lower valuation (P/S 0.8x), e.l.f. Beauty is recommended as the better buy due to its 30-quarter growth streak, strong earnings beat, successful Rhode acquisition, and accelerating momentum. Coupang faces headwinds including a major data breach affecting 33 million accounts, regulatory fines, and currency weakness.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company shows steady revenue growth (14.1% YoY) and profitability, it faces significant headwinds including a major data breach compromising 33 million accounts, regulatory fines, currency weakness, and geopolitical risks. The author notes it is 'managing headwinds' rather than accelerating.

The company demonstrates strong momentum with 30 consecutive quarters of sales growth (24.6% YoY), a significant earnings beat, successful Rhode acquisition integration, surging international revenue, and market share gains. The author explicitly recommends it as 'the stronger pick' for long-term investors due to accelerating growth and brand momentum.

title: Rhode Is Fueling e.l.f.'s Latest Surge. Is It Time to Jump In?
author: Geoffrey Seiler
description: e.l.f. Beauty reported strong fiscal Q1 results with 36% revenue growth to $479.4M, driven by its Rhode brand acquisition which contributed $160M in sales. The company raised full-year guidance and is expanding Rhode's distribution through Sephora and international markets while launching into hair care. With a forward P/E under 25, the analyst views the stock as having significant upside potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q1 earnings beat (36% revenue growth vs. consensus), significant guidance raises, successful Rhode acquisition contributing $160M in sales, multiple growth drivers (Sephora expansion, hair care entry, international expansion), and attractive valuation at forward P/E under 25 support positive outlook.
Mentioned only as a retail location where e.l.f.'s new hair care products launched. No direct impact on Target's business or performance discussed.

title: Why e.l.f. Beauty Stock Jumped 32% in June
author: Jennifer Saibil
description: e.l.f. Beauty stock surged 32% in June driven by anticipated tariff refunds of $58.5 million and the launch of a new hair care product line that generated 96% positive social media sentiment. The company continues to gain market share in cosmetics and skincare while maintaining strong sales growth of 35% year-over-year, though tariffs have pressured margins despite price increases.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 32% stock jump in June, 35% year-over-year sales growth, successful market share gains (9.2 percentage points in makeup), new hair care line with 96% positive sentiment, Rhode acquisition performing well, and potential $58.5 million tariff refund. Stock trades at reasonable 20x forward earnings despite being down year-to-date, presenting a buying opportunity for long-term investors.

title: These 3 Beaten-Down Growth Stocks Look Like Long-Term Comeback Candidates
author: John Ballard
description: Three consumer-focused growth stocks trading at discounts due to near-term macro headwinds present attractive long-term buying opportunities. Chewy benefits from a loyal customer base in a large pet industry with strong earnings growth expectations. Cava Group shows resilience with positive same-store sales and significant expansion runway compared to competitors. e.l.f. Beauty maintains market share gains and strong sales growth despite tariff pressures, with significant skincare expansion potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Trading at attractive 12x forward earnings with 32% annualized earnings growth expected. Strong customer loyalty (84% autoship sales), consistent net customer additions, and expansion into profitable pet healthcare services position it well for long-term growth despite near-term consumer spending pressure.

Demonstrating strong operational performance with 9.7% same-restaurant sales growth and positive comps for two consecutive years despite weak consumer environment. Significant expansion runway with only 459 locations versus Chipotle's 4,100+ locations, and 26% expected annual earnings growth supports long-term upside.

Seven consecutive years of market share gains with 25% net sales growth despite 22% year-to-date stock decline. Strong brand popularity, explosive skincare growth, and improving free cash flow ($190M trailing-12-month) suggest analyst expectations of 10% earnings growth are too conservative given expansion potential.
Mentioned as a comparable company with 4,100+ restaurants to highlight Cava's expansion opportunity. No direct investment recommendation or performance analysis provided in the article.

title: This Under-the-Radar Move Will Likely Drive e.l.f. Sales and Could Boost the Stock.
author: Geoffrey Seiler
description: e.l.f. Beauty unveiled new summer products for its Rhode brand, including three new items and limited-edition offerings. The expansion of Rhode's product assortment, combined with founder Hailey Bieber's social media promotion and higher profit margins, could drive significant sales growth. With a forward P/E of 16, the stock is considered undervalued with strong growth potential ahead.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article highlights Rhode's product expansion as a significant growth driver, notes the brand's higher profit margins compared to e.l.f.'s main line, emphasizes strong social media promotion by Hailey Bieber with 58 million followers, and values the stock at a reasonable forward P/E of 16 with substantial upside potential from future distribution expansion.
